 Brighton look dangerous but haven’t created much in the way of clear-cut chances. I assume at some point, Hurzeler will maker changes to get the win.
 Share 1m ago 13.32 EDT “No fan of the pink Sunderland kit,” emails Tim Smith, “but it gets a pass due to the absence of gaudy sponsorship across the front. It just looks cleaner to my eyes. Brighton’s throwback kit against Arsenal this season was a stunner, for the same reason. I’m a Leeds (and Adidas) fan, but the current sponsor/logo on the shirt makes it a dealbreaker for me.”
 Yeah, the Leeds logo is grim gear, but you accepts your money you takes your choice. And agree, the Brighton one is a work of art.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters Share 4m ago 13.30 EDT It’s quieter than it was in Poznan, Sunderland controlling midfield, but as I type, Danso, sent off at Bournemouth last Sunday, misses his kick and pulls Ishak down accordingly'; he’s booked. In better news for him, Black Sherif, his favourite Ghanaian singer – we saw him at a gig where my non-football-loving wife shamed me by recognising him – is coming to London on 4th December . I can’t recommend him highly enough – if you can get there, do it. Here’s a playlist to get you going.
 And here’s an interview. 
 ‘It’s created with a big red love!’: the ultra-inspirational music of Ghanaian star Black Sherif Read more Share 9m ago 13.24 EDT Rutter finds Osman at inside-left, a lovely ball arced down the line and inside. Inside the box, he shows the defender too much of the it but bundles through one challenge, only to stumble into the second and lose possession.
 Share 12m ago 13.22 EDT These Brighton players have loads to play for. Imagine the atmosphere around their training ground at the moment, and how much those not starting in the league want to force their way in. Given the struggles of various among the rich clubs, they’ve a proper chance of making top five – and who knows what else.
 Share 13m ago 13.20 EDT Rutter backs in inside the box and, expertly found by Gross, he controls and spins away from goal, his marker too tight, then lashes a shot just wide of the near post.
 Share 15m ago 13.18 EDT GOAL! Trabzonspor 1-0 Hearts (Salah pen 32)
 Salah watches Reus go right and clips over his legs and into the middle of the net.
 View image in fullscreen Trabzonspor's Mohamed Salah scores their first goal from the penalty spot. Photograph: Dilara Senkaya/Reuters Share Updated at  13.24 EDT 16m ago 13.17 EDT PENALTY TRABZONSPOR!
 31 min Franculino beats one man then another as he weaves into the box, Magnusson steps across him, and that’s an easy call for the ref.
 Share 19m ago 13.15 EDT Poznan are second in the Ekstraklasa, with 27 goals in 10 games, easily the most in the league, and they look likely tonight. I’d be shocked if this contest ends 0-1, but Sunderland should be good for at least one more goal too.
 Share 21m ago 13.13 EDT In Turkey, Trabzonspor are dominating against Hearts, but they’ve Andre Onana in goal and one can never be sure when he might toss one in: when Man United were last in the Champions League, they scored 12 goals in three matches against Bayern, Galatasaray twice and FCK, earning a single draw, largely because of his work in net.
 Share 25m ago 13.09 EDT Back in Poznan, Sunderland find Fofana, left side of the box, he shoots low and hard … hitting the far post! But the ball is then cut back to Xhaka who, eight yards out, should score. He sweeps goalwards … and straight at the keeper.
 Share 26m ago 13.08 EDT I guess he’s one of the first of the new guard of manager who had no playing career to speak of, but had a talent for understanding the game and where once, they’d have been a coach if that, now they’re running clubs. I’m certain we’ll see much more of this. Oh, but as I type, Verbruggen has to save sprawlingly at his near post.
 Share Updated at  13.08 EDT 28m ago 13.06 EDT Every time I’ve looked at Brighton, who show eight changes from their weekend win, they’ve got Jablonec boxed. The way Fabian Hurzeler has inculcated a style that allows players to come in and out without it changing, is exceptional.

 A cross to the back post is sent back across and Al-Taamari sticks away.
 View image in fullscreen Stade Rennes' Musa Al-Taamari (right) celebrates scoring their first goal. Photograph: Matteo Ciambelli/Reuters Share Updated at  13.20 EDT 30m ago 13.03 EDT GOAL! Sturm Graz 1-0 Marseille (Diakite 13)
 Three against Grazer at the weekend and now, the ball is given away in midfield, Weinhandl, the 17-year-old, wins it back, slides through the centre, and Diakite leans one way to slot confidently the other.
 View image in fullscreen Sturm Graz's Oumar Diakite (right) celebrates scoring the opening goal. Photograph: Erwin Scheriau/APA/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.19 EDT 34m ago 12.59 EDT And he’s playing well, pulling wide and crossing to win a corner. Back to the pink kit, given this is its second away outing in Europe, against teams with whom Sunderland’s colours don’t clash, we have to assume someone at the club is doing their best to make it legendary. It’d go nice with Frankfurt in May.
 Share 37m ago 12.57 EDT “It’s hard not to root for Timur Tutierov,” writes Kári Tulinius. “He is a Crimean Tatar refugee. He was just nine when Russia invaded and he fled with his family to Spain. Four years later they moved back to Ukraine. He’s never been back to his home.”
 Football is the greatest, part 67,907,336.
 Share 38m ago 12.56 EDT Sunderland fans in Poznan. I can only imagine the scenes, given a wild fanbase who feared they’d never get to do this.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Turner, G Share 40m ago 12.54 EDT GOAL! Juventus 1-0 Rennes (Celik 5)
 Don’t Juve need that. In loads of trouble, eighth in the league and with Luciano Spalletti fighting for his job, a lovely touch from McKennie allows Woltemade to send Celik though at inside-right, and he finishes confidently into the far corner.
 View image in fullscreen Zeki Celik fires home to give Juventus the lead. Photograph: Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.18 EDT 42m ago 12.52 EDT This is such an open game – twice, Poznan have been inside the Sunderland box looking dangerous, Roefs smothering one shot, just about.
 Share 43m ago 12.51 EDT That took 78 seconds – and remember, Sunderland scored at 90+3 of 90+5 in their last game against Torreense. The Prem, problems, but in Europe they’re flying!
 Share 44m ago 12.49 EDT GOAL! Lech Poznan 0-1 Sunderland (Tutierov 2)
 Poznan are bottom of the Europa League and already, we’ve seen why. The ball goes back to Lis, who sells Gurgul short with the ball out wide. Angulo snaps into the challenge, needs only one touch to set, and crosses for Tutierov to head home his first Sunderland goal!
 View image in fullscreen Sunderland's Timur Tutiero (right) celebrates after giving the visitors an early lead. Photograph: Wojtek Radwański/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.16 EDT 47m ago 12.47 EDT We’re under way in all our early games.

 Lech Poznan (4-2-3-1): Lis; Joel Pereira, Skrzypczak, Yegebe, Gurgul; Murawski, Kozubal; Wålemark, Rodriguez, Hakans; Ishak. Subs: Obremski, Pruchniewski,Bergrren, Agnero, Bengtsson, Jagiello, Bartczak, Szymczak, Palma, Janyska.
 Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs; Mukiele, Danso, O’Nien, Methalie; Xhaka, Ahokal; Angulo, Diarra, Fofana; Tutierov. Subs: Moore, Rigg, Alderete, Reinildo, Sadiki, Le Fee, Hume, Whittaker, Ogunsuyi, Jones, Scott, Proctor.
 Share 1h ago 12.18 EDT OH MY COMPLETE AND UTTER EVERLOVING DAYS! 
 Sri Lanka stun England by chasing down 430 to win as ODI records tumble – live Read more Share 2h ago 11.15 EDT Preamble
 It’s been a strange start to the season for Sunderland and I’m not just talking about those pink Elvis kits. Yes, that is a real sentence. They’ve had some rotten luck – if they could’ve picked two players to avoid injury, Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey would probably have been them – and, after last season’s outrageous exploits, they now sit bottom of the Premier League.
 However! Making their first foray into Europe in 52 years, they won their first home game then, on their first trip abroad, they conceded a ridiculous opener, equalised, had a late penalty confiscated … and scored an incredible injury-time winner which was also Noah Sadiki’s first goal for the club, all of which combined into one of the great away-end goons. And no, I’m not enumerating it in such detail because my best mate had to cry off late doors due to a work crisis, I promise; by way of compensation, I’ve demanded he furnish us with photos from Poznan.
 So, Sunderland’s trip to Poland will form the centrepiece of our early coverage, but that’s not the half of what we’ve got going on. Little more than a decade ago, if someone told us Milan were going to Bournemouth, we’d have assumed it was in holiday and told them not to miss Sega World or Splashdown in Poole. Now, though, they’re visiting for a game of football, one of the biggest ever played in the town, and Dean Court will be bouncing for what is our featured match in the second part of the evening.
 View image in fullscreen Milan fans on Bournemouth pier earlier on Thursday. Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images And, in among all of that, we’ve got Crystal Palace’s trip to Besiktas and one of the great – not a word I use lightly in this context – town centre grounds, plus the linguistic derby of Celtic v Celta, Juventus v Rennes, and form team Brighton’s jaunt to Jablonec in the Conference.
 Kick-offs: 5.45pm BST and 8pm BST
